name: Jerzens
kurzbeschreibung: Sunny hamlet in the Pitztal valley with lift access to the ski area and the idyllic Pitz-taler Sonnenseite.
beschreibung:
Overview

Jerzens is situated at an elevation of 1,107 metres in the front Pitztal Valley within the district of Imst, in the Tyrolean Oberland. This scenic mountain community sits gracefully upon a sun-drenched plateau along the eastern valley slopes beneath the iconic Hochzeiger peak (2,560 m), home to approximately 920 residents. Blessed with a protected hillside orientation, Jerzens is celebrated as the sunniest village in the entire Pitztal. The municipality spans from the valley floor along the Pitze river (900 m) past the lift base of Liss (1,450 m) up to Mount Wildgrat at 2,971 metres. Home to one of the largest ancient Swiss stone pine (Zirbe) forests in the Northern Alps, Jerzens seamlessly combines genuine alpine farming traditions with state-of-the-art mountain recreation, delighting families and outdoor enthusiasts year-round.

History

Archaeological evidence confirms the existence of a high-medieval fortified settlement at Burgstall Niederhof around 1200. The village was first documented in 1313 in a land registry of the Imst provincial court under the name Irtzens, which likely traces back to ancient Rhaeto-Romanic roots. For centuries, the Cistercian Abbey of Stams held extensive feudal rights over the parish, an heritage still commemorated in the municipal coat of arms. The spiritual centerpiece of the village is the Parish Church of St. Gotthard, constructed in 1736–1737 by Gallus Gratl and dedicated to Bishop Gotthard of Hildesheim—an exceptionally rare dedication across Tyrol. Inside, visitors can admire late-Baroque altarpieces and a valuable late-Gothic wood relief of the Lamentation of Christ from 1520. In 1966, local mountain farmers pooled their resources to build the Hochzeiger cableways, halting depopulation and inaugurating the modern tourism era.

Getting There

Jerzens offers straightforward road and public transit connectivity. Motorists arrive via the Inntal Motorway A12 taking the Imst/Pitztal exit, or toll-free from Germany via the B179 Fernpass road into Imst. From Imst, follow the Pitztal provincial road L16 to Wenns, turning onto the L241 Jerzen road which climbs to the village and the Liss lift terminal in about 15 minutes. Rail travellers arrive at Imst-Pitztal railway station, served by Austrian Railjet and Eurocity trains. Directly outside the terminal, regional bus line 4204 provides frequent connections straight to Jerzens village square and the Hochzeiger valley station.

Tips

The premier recreational focal point is the Hochzeiger ski and hiking mountain. In summer, the ZirbenPark at the 2,000-metre mid-station is unmissable: Families explore 17 interactive stations along the Swiss Stone Pine Trail, climb the 12-metre-high cone-shaped viewing tower with its spiral slide, and zoom downhill on three-wheeled ZirbenCarts over a thrilling 3.7-kilometre track. In winter, the Hochzeiger ski domain features 40 kilometres of groomed runs ascending to 2,450 metres alongside a floodlit six-kilometre natural toboggan run. Hikers seeking quiet solitude can venture into the pristine Riegetal valley in the Kaunergrat Nature Park to explore the crystal-clear waters of Großsee and Schwarzsee.
